processing: A baked (hong qing) green tea: fixed, then dried with hot air instead of being pan-finished. The orchid note is natural, with no flower scenting.
harvest_season: Spring, as usual for Anhui greens.
appearance_dry: Open, emerald leaf, shaped a little like an orchid.
appearance_wet: Tender, even green leaf, typical of a baked Anhui green.
taste_profile: Fresh and mellow with a sweet return, and a clean, lasting orchid fragrance.

brewing.notes: As with other baked greens, keep the water cool and the leaf light: an open leaf extracts quickly.

vintage_note: As with other Anhui greens, it is sold as the current spring's harvest and is best within about a year. Look for the Tongcheng name and a picking date, since the tea is little known outside its region.
description:
Tongcheng Xiaohua is a baked green from the hills of Tongcheng, in Anqing on the southeastern side of the Dabie Mountains. Its calling card is an orchid fragrance that comes from the place and the leaf, not from flowers added to the tea.

It is baked with hot air after fixing, not pan-finished as Long Jing is, and that gentler finish keeps the leaf open and the aroma clean. The protected area lies in the hills of the northwest of the county.

The cup is bright tender green, fresh and mellow with a sweet finish.

The protected area covers 33 villages in seven towns and subdistricts. Buy the current spring, and try it side by side with Shucheng Xiaolanhua to see how two neighbours take on the orchid idea.
history:
Sources place its creation in the Ming and say it was sent as tribute in the Ming and Qing, though these claims come from secondary accounts and not from a named early text.

In modern times it has been recognised as a regional product, with an agricultural geographical indication reported from 2018.
